# Design Document ## Overview The project-showcase feature adds a Velite-driven `projects` collection plus two server-rendered routes — the gallery at `/projects` and per-project detail pages at `/projects/[slug]` — to the existing static-first Next.js site. The collection accepts colocated MDX files under `content/projects/`, validates frontmatter via Velite, and emits typed records that consumers reach through a single chokepoint module `src/lib/projects.ts`. The detail page renders the MDX body inside Tailwind Typography's `prose` class within a `max-w-5xl` outer container, with a fixed list of seven wide-media tags (`img`, `video`, `pre`, `figure`, `table`, `iframe`, `svg`) escaping the prose column via Tailwind Typography's selective-element-width pattern. The gallery presents reverse-chronological cards keyed on the cover image, with above-the-fold cards loading eagerly and below-the-fold cards lazy-loading. A shared date helper at `src/lib/format-date.ts` extracts the formatter currently inlined in `src/lib/blog.ts`; the blog re-exports the helper so `formatPostDate === formatContentDate` at runtime. The design is entirely additive to site-foundation, blog-core, and professional-profile. The existing `pages`, `profile`, and `posts` Velite collections, the `` renderer, the shadcn `Card` primitive, the site-wide CSP, the `next-themes` setup, the rehype/remark plugin chains, and the `BLOG_INCLUDE_DRAFTS` draft-leak guard pattern are reused. The only new client-side surface is zero — both new routes are server-rendered, statically generated, and ship no incremental client JavaScript. One fixture project (`fixture-placeholder.mdx` under `draft: true`) is committed in the same PR as the collection registration so CI's empty-collection contract test has a substrate without forcing a real project to ship before the spec lands. ## Steering Document Alignment ### Technical Standards (tech.md) - **Markdown-driven content pipeline (tech.md §"Content Pipeline")**: the new `projects` collection follows the established Velite pattern from `pages`, `profile`, and `posts` — frontmatter-validated MDX, build-time compilation, zero runtime cost. Schema uses Velite's `s.image()` primitive for cover/og image processing (asset copy, dimension extraction); the dimension/file-size band is enforced in the `.transform()` step after Velite returns the resolved image metadata. - **TypeScript strict mode (tech.md §"Core Technologies")**: all new modules (`src/lib/projects.ts`, `src/lib/format-date.ts`, `src/lib/project-errors.ts`) are TypeScript with strict-mode types. The chokepoint scanner uses the `typescript` package's compiler API (already a dev dependency). - **No client-side JavaScript libraries (tech.md §"Application Architecture")**: gallery and detail pages are server components. The "Featured" accent treatment is pure CSS. No animation libraries, no client hydration. - **shadcn/ui primitives (tech.md §"Styling")**: gallery cards reuse the shadcn `Card`, `CardHeader`, `CardContent` primitives already used by `PostCard` in `src/components/blog/post-card.tsx`. - **Tailwind Typography (tech.md §"Styling")**: detail-page body styling uses the `prose` class already in use on `/blog/[slug]`. The seven wide-media tags are NOT width-constrained by `prose` because Typography v0.5's class targets text-flow elements (`p`, `h2`–`h6`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `blockquote`, `hr`) and leaves media elements (`img`, `video`, `pre`, `figure`, `table`, `iframe`, `svg`) at the parent container's width by default. This is the selective-element-width-constraint pattern referenced in Req 6.7 — no custom CSS, no `100vw`/negative-margin hacks. - **Velite v0.3.1 API (tech.md §"Content Pipeline")**: `s.image()` is the standard image primitive; its output shape is `{ src: string, width: number, height: number, blurDataURL?: string }` (verified against `node_modules/velite/dist/index.d.ts`). The output-shape contract test (Req 1.11) freezes this assumption at the spec boundary. ### Project Structure (structure.md) - **Content directory**: `content/projects/.mdx`, matching structure.md's documented `content/projects/` layout. Colocated assets allowed either as flat siblings (`content/projects/my-project.mdx` + `content/projects/my-project-cover.png`) or per-project subdirectory (`content/projects/my-project/index.mdx` + `content/projects/my-project/cover.png`). Velite resolves both. - **Route layout**: `src/app/(site)/projects/page.tsx` (gallery) and `src/app/(site)/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` (detail) — matches the structure.md `(site)/projects/` placeholder. The existing `PlaceholderPage`-based `page.tsx` at `src/app/(site)/projects/page.tsx` is replaced; the `[slug]/page.tsx` is added. - **Library modules**: `src/lib/projects.ts` and `src/lib/projects.test.ts` parallel `src/lib/blog.ts`/`src/lib/blog.test.ts`. `src/lib/format-date.ts` and `src/lib/format-date.test.ts` are new shared modules. `src/lib/project-errors.ts` mirrors `src/lib/blog-errors.ts`. - **Component modules**: `src/components/projects/project-card.tsx`, `src/components/projects/link-rail.tsx`, `src/components/projects/status-badge.tsx`. Each is a single-responsibility server component. - **Documentation**: `docs/projects-authoring.md` and `docs/projects-authoring.test.ts` (or `tests/docs/projects-authoring.test.ts` per repo convention; chosen path documented in tasks). - **Sitemap extension**: `src/app/sitemap.ts` is extended to include `/projects/` entries derived from `getPublishedProjects()`. - **Fixture canary**: `src/__fixtures__/chokepoint-canary.ts` — INSIDE the scanner's scan path (Req 7.6.h), excluded from the TypeScript build via `tsconfig.json` `exclude`. ## Code Reuse Analysis ### Existing Components to Leverage - **`src/components/shared/mdx-content.tsx`** (``): renders Velite-compiled MDX bodies via `new Function(code)(runtime)`. Used unchanged for the detail-page body. The implicit "no `components` argument" behavior is the foundation of Req 6.9.d (no custom component registry) — capitalized JSX tag references like `` throw `ReferenceError` at static-generation time, which Next.js surfaces as a build failure. - **`src/components/ui/card.tsx`** (``, ``, ``): used by the new `` (parallel to ``). - **`src/lib/blog.ts`** — the date-formatter literal at `src/lib/blog.ts:86–94` is extracted to `src/lib/format-date.ts`. `blog.ts` re-exports the helper: `export const formatPostDate = formatContentDate;` (Req 9.2). - **`src/lib/blog-errors.ts`**: the `checkVercelDraftGuard()` pattern, the `VERCEL_ENV_VAR_NAME` / `VERCEL_FLAG_VAR_NAME` constants, and the looks-like-prod logic are mirrored into `src/lib/project-errors.ts`. The two modules remain separate (one per content type) rather than fused; this matches Req 12's "pattern reuse over abstraction — three collections too few to amortize." - **`velite.config.ts`**: the `sharedRemarkPlugins` / `sharedRehypePlugins` arrays and the `prettyCodeOptions` constant are reused for the new collection's MDX pipeline. The new `projects` collection is added to the `collections` map alongside `pages`, `profile`, `posts`. - **`src/app/sitemap.ts`**: existing module is extended; `/projects` was already in the static route list, and per-project URLs are appended from `getPublishedProjects()`. - **`@/lib/build/derive-post-slug.mjs`** pattern (not the function itself, which is post-specific): the slug-derivation pattern of `s.path()` + `.transform()` stripping the collection prefix is replicated for `projects`. ### Integration Points - **Velite output (`#site/content` alias)**: the new collection exports `projects` from `.velite/index.js`. All access is funnelled through `src/lib/projects.ts`; the chokepoint test enforces this for all four import shapes (named, namespace, barrel, dynamic). - **Next.js Image (`next/image`)**: gallery cards and detail-page cover images flow through the existing Next.js Image pipeline (WebP/AVIF, responsive `sizes`, lazy-load below the fold). No new config in `next.config.ts` because `/static/...` is already served from the same domain as the site (CSP unchanged). - **Sitemap**: `src/app/sitemap.ts` consumes `getPublishedProjects()` and appends entries with `lastModified: project.updated ?? project.date`. - **Internal link checker** (already runs in CI for blog routes): naturally picks up the new project subtree. ## Architecture The feature is a three-layer stack: (1) Velite collection + transform at build time; (2) chokepoint query module + draft-leak guard at server-render time; (3) two route components plus three presentational components at render time. A build-time remark check enforces MDX heading hygiene before the body reaches Velite's MDX compiler. A TypeScript-compiler-API-based chokepoint scanner runs in CI to enforce the single-import-path contract. A canary fixture exercises the scanner against all four forbidden patterns. ```mermaid graph TD A[content/projects/*.mdx] --> B[Velite projects collection
+ frontmatter schema
+ s.image cover/og
+ remark heading-hygiene check] B --> C[.velite/projects.json] C --> D[src/lib/projects.ts
getPublishedProjects
shouldShowUpdatedBadge
byDateDescSlugAsc] D --> E[src/app/(site)/projects/page.tsx
Gallery] D --> F[src/app/(site)/projects/[slug]/page.tsx
Detail] D --> G[src/app/sitemap.ts] E --> H[ProjectCard] E --> I[StatusBadge] F --> J[LinkRail] F --> K[StatusBadge] F --> L[MDXContent] M[src/lib/format-date.ts
formatContentDate] --> D M --> N[src/lib/blog.ts
re-exports as formatPostDate] O[src/lib/project-errors.ts
checkVercelDraftGuard
draft-leak messages] --> D P[src/__fixtures__/chokepoint-canary.ts] -.canary test.-> Q[runChokepointScan] Q -.CI gate.-> D ``` ### Modular Design Principles - **Single File Responsibility**: - `src/lib/projects.ts` — query functions ONLY (no rendering, no JSX, no DOM). - `src/lib/format-date.ts` — `formatContentDate` ONLY. - `src/lib/project-errors.ts` — draft-leak guard helpers and message constants ONLY. - `src/components/projects/project-card.tsx` — gallery card layout ONLY. - `src/components/projects/link-rail.tsx` — link-rail rendering ONLY. - `src/components/projects/status-badge.tsx` — status badge rendering ONLY. - **Component Isolation**: `` does not import `` (Req 5.6 — rail only on detail page). `` does not know about ``. `` is used by both card and detail page. - **Service Layer Separation**: `src/lib/projects.ts` is the only consumer of `#site/content`'s `projects` export. Page components consume `src/lib/projects.ts`. The chokepoint test enforces this with the TypeScript compiler API. - **Utility Modularity**: `formatContentDate` lives at `src/lib/format-date.ts` (not buried in `projects.ts` or `blog.ts`). The `byDateDescSlugAsc` comparator lives at the top of `src/lib/projects.ts` (parallel to `blog.ts:18`). ## Components and Interfaces ### Component 1: Velite `projects` collection - **Purpose**: validate frontmatter and process cover/og images at build time; compile MDX body; enforce heading hygiene. - **Location**: `velite.config.ts` (the `projects` collection definition is added alongside `pages`, `profile`, `posts`). - **Schema (TypeScript-equivalent, lifted from Req 1.2 and Req 1.3)**: ```ts s.object({ title: s.string().min(1).max(120), description: s.string().min(50).max(160), // meta description ONLY summary: s.string().min(30).max(140), // gallery card ONLY date: s.isodate(), cover: s.image(), // dimensions/size checked in transform coverAlt: s.string().min(1).max(250), tags: s.array(s.string().regex(/^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/)).max(8).default([]), status: s.enum(["active", "archived", "concept"]).default("active"), ogImage: s.image().optional(), // dimensions/aspect checked in transform updated: s.isodate().optional(), draft: s.boolean().default(false), slug: s.path(), featured: s.boolean().default(false), links: s.array(linkSchema).max(6).optional(), // see linkSchema below body: s.mdx(), }).strict() ``` where `linkSchema` is: ```ts s.object({ kind: s.enum(["demo", "repo", "docs", "package", "writeup"]).optional(), label: s.string().min(1).max(60), url: s.string(), }) ``` - **Transform step responsibilities** (executes after Velite's schema parse, before `.velite/projects.json` write): 1. Strip the `projects/` prefix from the auto-derived `slug` (when frontmatter `slug` is absent). 2. Validate `cover` dimensions: `width >= 1200`, `height >= 800`. Validate `cover` file size: warn at 500 KB, fail at 1 MB (read from `meta.path`-derived absolute, `fs.statSync`). 3. Validate `ogImage` (when present): `width >= 1200`, aspect within 1.72–2.10. **When `ogImage` is absent for a non-draft project**: emit an INFO-level log line to `process.stdout` naming the slug and stating that share previews will use the site default (Req 1.3). 4. Validate `links` (when present): URL parses via `new URL()`, protocol is `http:` or `https:`, `kind` uniqueness enforced (Req 5.1). Error messages include file path, array index, and the bad value; the `kind`-rejection message follows the exact contract in Req 5.1. 5. Run the MDX heading-hygiene check against the body's MDX AST (see Component 2 below). - **Plugin pipeline**: `mdx`/`markdown` top-level config already declares `sharedRemarkPlugins` / `sharedRehypePlugins`. The new collection inherits these automatically — no per-collection plugin config. - **Interfaces**: emits `projects: Project[]` from `.velite/`. The `Project` type is derived as `(typeof projects)[number]`. - **Dependencies**: `velite`, `s.image()`, `s.mdx()`, the shared remark/rehype plugin arrays, `unified`/`remark-parse`/`remark-mdx`/`unist-util-visit` (for the heading-hygiene check), `node:fs`. - **Reuses**: `velite.config.ts`'s existing structure; the `posts` collection's `.transform((data, { meta }) => …)` pattern. ### Component 2: MDX heading-hygiene check - **Purpose**: AST-only enforcement of Req 6.9.a (no `

`), Req 6.9.b (no h4+ unless `PROJECTS_ALLOW_H4=1`), Req 6.9.c (h2-first, no level skips). - **Location**: helper function inside `velite.config.ts` (or extracted to `src/lib/build/check-project-headings.ts` if the helper grows beyond ~80 lines). Invoked from the `projects` collection's `.transform()`. - **AST walking**: 1. `unified().use(remarkParse).use(remarkGfm).use(remarkMdx).parse(content)` — content is `meta.content` (frontmatter-stripped body, available on Velite's `VeliteFile`). 2. `unist-util-visit` traverses the tree in document order. 3. For each `heading` node (mdast core): record `depth`. 4. For each `mdxJsxFlowElement` and `mdxJsxTextElement` whose tag name (case-insensitively) equals `h1`: rejection per Req 6.9.a. 5. **Code-fence safety**: nodes of type `code` (fenced) and `inlineCode` are never visited for heading concerns — `

` inside a fenced code block exists as a `code` node's `value` string, NOT as a `heading` or `mdxJsxFlowElement` node. This is the AST-only contract from Req 6.9.a. - **Heading-sequence enforcement (Req 6.9.c)**: 1. Collect the linear sequence of `depth` values from `heading` nodes in document order. 2. If the sequence is empty: pass. 3. If `sequence[0] !== 2`: fail with `"[velite/projects] {file}: first heading must be h2 (found h{depth}); see Req 6.9.c"`. 4. Walk the sequence pairwise: if `next > prev + 1`, fail with `"[velite/projects] {file}: heading skip from h{prev} to h{next}; see Req 6.9.c"` (unless `prev` is `0`-equivalent — there is no `prev=0` case because the first heading is already gated to h2). 5. `PROJECTS_ALLOW_H4` semantics: when unset, h4+ headings (depth ≥ 4) fail with the Req 6.9.b error. When `=1`, h4+ headings are stderr-warned (matching the `posts` collection's `BLOG_ALLOW_H4=1` pattern) AND the heading-skip check still runs (an h2 → h4 skip remains a build failure even with `PROJECTS_ALLOW_H4=1` set — the env var unlocks the depth, NOT the sequence). - **Interfaces**: pure function `checkProjectHeadings(content: string, fileRel: string): void` — throws on rejection, returns void on pass. - **Dependencies**: `unified`, `remark-parse`, `remark-gfm`, `remark-mdx`, `unist-util-visit`. - **Reuses**: the same plugin stack that `velite.config.ts` already imports for the `posts` collection's rejection visitor. ### Component 3: `src/lib/projects.ts` (chokepoint module) - **Purpose**: single import path for the `projects` collection. Applies draft filter, supplies sort, derives badges. - **Public surface**: ```ts export type Project = (typeof projects)[number]; export type ProjectLink = NonNullable[number]; export function getPublishedProjects(): Project[]; export function getProjectBySlug(slug: string): Project | null; export function shouldShowUpdatedBadge(project: Project): boolean; // formatContentDate is re-exported from src/lib/format-date.ts at the call site // (consumers import it directly from format-date.ts; projects.ts does NOT re-export). ``` - **`getPublishedProjects()`** mirrors `getPublishedPosts()` structure (`src/lib/blog.ts:24–50`): 1. `checkVercelDraftGuard()` from `src/lib/project-errors.ts` — throws on `production+drafts` or `preview+!drafts` or looks-like-prod. 2. `const includeDrafts = process.env.PROJECTS_INCLUDE_DRAFTS === "1";` 3. **Build-log warning (Req 7.2.c)**: when `includeDrafts && process.env.NODE_ENV === "production"`, write a clearly visible warning line to `process.stderr` naming each draft slug. This is the build-time-surfacing contract. 4. `const filtered = includeDrafts ? projects : projects.filter((p) => !p.draft);` 5. `return [...filtered].sort(byDateDescSlugAsc);` - **`shouldShowUpdatedBadge(project)`**: `project.updated != null && new Date(project.updated) > new Date(project.date)` — identical predicate to the post variant. - **`byDateDescSlugAsc`**: lives at top-of-file, internal (not exported as part of the public surface). - **Interfaces**: only the public surface above; consumers of `#site/content` outside `src/lib/projects.ts` are CI errors via the chokepoint test. - **Dependencies**: `#site/content`, `src/lib/project-errors.ts`, `src/lib/format-date.ts` (consumers import it via this module's re-export only for stability — see "decision on re-export" below). - **Decision on re-export of `formatContentDate`**: `src/lib/projects.ts` does NOT re-export `formatContentDate`. Page components and tests import it directly from `src/lib/format-date.ts`. Rationale: re-exporting would create a second name (`projects.formatContentDate` aliased to `format-date.formatContentDate`) and tempt a future maintainer to localize the function. Keep ONE canonical import path per helper. This is the symmetric inverse of the `blog.ts` re-export: blog re-exports as `formatPostDate` because the `formatPostDate` name was the pre-existing public API of blog.ts (Req 9.2 explicitly requires the parity test). Projects has no analogous legacy API. - **Reuses**: `src/lib/blog.ts`'s shape; nothing physically reused at the module-instance level (separate per-content-type modules). ### Component 4: `src/lib/format-date.ts` (shared formatter) - **Purpose**: single source of truth for content-date formatting. - **Public surface**: ```ts const contentDateFormatter = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-CA", { year: "numeric", month: "long", day: "numeric", }); export function formatContentDate(iso: string): { datetime: string; display: string } { return { datetime: iso, display: contentDateFormatter.format(new Date(iso)) }; } ``` - **Migration path**: existing inline definition at `src/lib/blog.ts:81–94` (`postDateFormatter` + `formatPostDate`) is replaced by: ```ts import { formatContentDate } from "@/lib/format-date"; export const formatPostDate = formatContentDate; ``` - **Parity test** at `src/lib/format-date.test.ts`: - Asserts `formatContentDate("2026-05-25").display === "May 25, 2026"` (English-Canada formatter output). - Imports `formatPostDate` from `@/lib/blog` and asserts `formatPostDate === formatContentDate` by reference. - **Interfaces**: pure function. No I/O. No side effects. - **Dependencies**: `Intl.DateTimeFormat` (built-in). - **Reuses**: the exact formatter literal from `src/lib/blog.ts:82–86`. ### Component 5: `src/lib/project-errors.ts` (draft-leak guard) - **Purpose**: mirror `src/lib/blog-errors.ts` for the projects collection. Keep error-message content next to the variable names that compose it. - **Public surface**: ```ts export const PROJECTS_DRAFT_FLAG_VAR_NAME = "PROJECTS_INCLUDE_DRAFTS"; export const PROJECTS_DRAFT_LEAK_GUARD_MSG_PRODUCTION = `[project-showcase] Draft projects are visible in a Vercel production build. ...`; export const PROJECTS_DRAFT_LEAK_GUARD_MSG_PREVIEW = `[project-showcase] Preview builds are running without drafts. ...`; export function checkVercelDraftGuard(): { kind: "production" | "preview" } | null; ``` - **Logic (identical shape to `blog-errors.ts`)**: ```ts function checkVercelDraftGuard() { const vercel = process.env.VERCEL; const env = process.env.VERCEL_ENV; const drafts = process.env.PROJECTS_INCLUDE_DRAFTS; if (vercel !== "1") return null; if (env === "production" && drafts === "1") return { kind: "production" }; if (env === "preview" && drafts !== "1") return { kind: "preview" }; // Looks-like-prod fail-closed (Req 7.3): when VERCEL=1 but VERCEL_ENV is empty/absent/unrecognized, // treat as production for guard purposes. if (env !== "preview" && env !== "production" && drafts === "1") return { kind: "production" }; return null; } ``` The looks-like-prod branch is the addition over `blog-errors.ts` and explicitly covers Req 7.3's "fail closed on ambiguity." (A follow-up refactor may unify the two `-errors.ts` files; deferred — see Deferrals below.) - **Interfaces**: pure function + string constants. - **Reuses**: pattern from `src/lib/blog-errors.ts`. ### Component 6: `` - **Purpose**: gallery card rendering. - **Location**: `src/components/projects/project-card.tsx`. - **Props**: ```ts type ProjectCardProps = { project: Project; eager: boolean; // controls Next.js Image `priority`/`loading` for above/below-the-fold cards }; ``` - **DOM structure (Req 2.3 DOM order)**: ```tsx

{project.title}

{display} {project.status !== "active" ? : null} {project.featured ? Featured : null}

{project.summary}
``` - **Accessibility (Req 2.6)**: single anchor; `aria-labelledby` scopes the link's accessible name to the title only. - **Featured treatment (Req 2.7)**: accent border + subtle background tint via a `featured` CSS class. **NO grid-column-span change, NO row-order change, NO size change** — Tailwind classes applied conditionally are limited to `border-`, `bg-`, and `ring-` utilities. The gallery grid uses `auto-rows: auto` so a featured card with a slightly heavier border does not shift its own row height meaningfully; the chronological sort order is established BEFORE the card is rendered, so the data plumbing is unaffected. The "Featured" textual badge appears in the card header. - **`eager` plumbing**: the gallery page computes `eager = index < firstRowSize` where `firstRowSize` is hardcoded at 4 (covers desktop multi-column; on tablet that's 2 rows of 2 = 4 cards, also acceptable for an above-the-fold approximation; on mobile single-column that's 4 cards' worth of vertical scroll, all loading eagerly is acceptable for ≤4 covers at <500 KB each). This is a heuristic, not exact viewport detection — server-rendered components do not know the viewport. - **Reuses**: ``, ``, `` from `src/components/ui/card.tsx`; `next/image`; `formatContentDate` from `src/lib/format-date.ts`. ### Component 7: `` - **Purpose**: textual status indicator on cards and the detail page. - **Location**: `src/components/projects/status-badge.tsx`. - **Props**: `{ status: "archived" | "concept" }` — `active` callers do not render the component at all (Req 4.2). - **DOM**: a plain `` with a status-specific class. Plain rendered text in static HTML. No JS. (Req 4.5.) - **Reuses**: nothing structural. ### Component 8: `` - **Purpose**: detail-page external links. - **Location**: `src/components/projects/link-rail.tsx`. - **Props**: `{ links: ProjectLink[] }`. Caller (detail page) checks `links && links.length > 0` BEFORE rendering — the component itself does not render an empty rail (defense in depth). - **DOM**: ```tsx
    {links.map((link, i) => (
  • {link.label}
    • ))}
``` - Display order is array order (Req 5.4). - Same-tab (no `target="_blank"`) — Req 5.5. - `rel="noopener"`; `noreferrer` intentionally omitted — Req 5.5. - **Icon handling**: when `kind` is set (recognized enum), an icon component is rendered alongside the label. The icon is a server-rendered inline SVG (no client JS). Icon selection: `demo` → external-link icon; `repo` → git-fork icon; `docs` → book icon; `package` → box icon; `writeup` → document icon. Concrete SVG choices are a tasks-phase decision; the contract here is "kind drives icon, label is always present, kind-less entries render label-only." - **Position (Req 5.4)**: rail appears ABOVE the MDX body on the detail page. - **Reuses**: nothing structural. ### Component 9: Gallery page `src/app/(site)/projects/page.tsx` - **Purpose**: render the reverse-chronological card grid (Req 2). - **Server component**. `export const dynamic = "force-static";` (Req 2.2). - **Structure**: ```tsx export const dynamic = "force-static"; export const metadata: Metadata = { title: "Projects", description: "Projects Matthew has built.", }; export default function ProjectsPage() { const projects = getPublishedProjects(); if (projects.length === 0) { return ; // Req 2.9 } return (

Projects

    {projects.map((project, i) => (
    • ))}
); } ``` - **Empty state (Req 2.9)**: renders `

No projects published yet.

Check back later.

`. Returns 200, not 404. - **Reuses**: `src/lib/projects.ts`; the page-layout wrapper pattern from `src/app/(site)/blog/page.tsx`. ### Component 10: Detail page `src/app/(site)/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` - **Purpose**: render a single project's detail (Req 6). - **Server component**. `export const dynamic = "force-static";`. `export const dynamicParams = false;` (matches blog). - **Structure**: ```tsx export const dynamic = "force-static"; export const dynamicParams = false; export function generateStaticParams() { return getPublishedProjects().map((p) => ({ slug: p.slug })); } export async function generateMetadata({ params }) { const { slug } = await params; const project = getProjectBySlug(slug); if (!project) return {}; const metadata: Metadata = { title: project.title, description: project.description, // meta-only field, Req 6.4 alternates: { canonical: `/projects/${project.slug}` }, openGraph: { type: "article", title: project.title, description: project.description, publishedTime: project.date, ...(project.updated ? { modifiedTime: project.updated } : {}), ...(project.ogImage ? { images: [{ url: project.ogImage.src, width: project.ogImage.width, height: project.ogImage.height }] } : {}), }, }; return metadata; } export default async function ProjectPage({ params }) { const { slug } = await params; const project = getProjectBySlug(slug); if (!project) notFound(); const { datetime, display } = formatContentDate(project.date); return (

{project.title}

{display} {shouldShowUpdatedBadge(project) ? : null} {project.status !== "active" ? : null}
{project.links && project.links.length > 0 ? : null}
Back to all projects
); } ``` - **Container-width contract (Req 6.7)**: outer is `max-w-5xl` (1024 px / 64 rem) centered with `mx-auto`. The MDX body sits inside `prose`. The seven wide-media tags (`img`, `video`, `pre`, `figure`, `table`, `iframe`, `svg`) are NOT width-constrained by Tailwind Typography's `prose` class — they fill the parent container (the `prose` div, which is constrained to `max-w-5xl` via its parent). The text-flow elements inside `prose` constrain to ~65ch via Typography's default styles. RTL-safe (no negative margins, no `100vw`), scrollbar-safe (no viewport-relative units). - **``**: inline span rendered when `shouldShowUpdatedBadge(project)` is true. Renders "Updated on {formatContentDate(project.updated).display}". Defined as a local component inside the page file — not extracted (single-use). - **Reuses**: ``, `next/image`, `notFound`, `src/lib/projects.ts`, `src/lib/format-date.ts`. ### Component 11: Chokepoint enforcement test - **Purpose**: CI gate that fails the build when any file outside the allowlist imports `projects` from `#site/content` (Req 7.4). - **Location**: `src/lib/projects.test.ts` (test); the scanner function is internal to the test file or lifted to `src/lib/build/check-projects-chokepoint.ts` if reused. - **Algorithm (TypeScript compiler API)**: ```ts function runChokepointScan(filePath: string): ScanFinding[] { const source = fs.readFileSync(filePath, "utf8"); const sf = ts.createSourceFile(filePath, source, ts.ScriptTarget.Latest, true); const findings: ScanFinding[] = []; function visit(node: ts.Node) { // (a) named import if (ts.isImportDeclaration(node) && isContentSpecifier(node.moduleSpecifier)) { const named = node.importClause?.namedBindings; if (named && ts.isNamedImports(named)) { for (const el of named.elements) { if (el.propertyName?.escapedText === "projects" || el.name.escapedText === "projects") { findings.push({ kind: "named", node: el }); } } } // (b) namespace import — flag entire `* as content` then later look for content.projects if (named && ts.isNamespaceImport(named)) { const localName = named.name.escapedText.toString(); // record namespace alias; second pass through the AST checks for `localName.projects` recordNamespace(filePath, localName); } // (c) barrel re-export } if (ts.isExportDeclaration(node) && isContentSpecifier(node.moduleSpecifier)) { // `export * from "#site/content"` OR `export { projects } from "#site/content"` findings.push({ kind: "barrel", node }); } // (d) dynamic import if ((ts.isCallExpression(node) && node.expression.kind === ts.SyntaxKind.ImportKeyword) || (ts.isCallExpression(node) && ts.isIdentifier(node.expression) && node.expression.escapedText === "require")) { const arg = node.arguments[0]; if (arg && isContentSpecifierLiteralOrTemplate(arg)) { findings.push({ kind: "dynamic", node }); } } ts.forEachChild(node, visit); } visit(sf); // second pass for namespace-then-member references if (hasRecordedNamespace(filePath)) { ts.forEachChild(sf, function visit2(n) { if (ts.isPropertyAccessExpression(n) && ts.isIdentifier(n.expression) && isRecordedNamespace(filePath, n.expression.escapedText.toString()) && n.name.escapedText === "projects") { findings.push({ kind: "namespace", node: n }); } ts.forEachChild(n, visit2); }); } return findings; } ``` - `isContentSpecifier(specifier)`: returns true for the string-literal `"#site/content"` AND for template-literal expressions whose static parts cover the alias. - `isContentSpecifierLiteralOrTemplate(arg)`: handles both `import("#site/content")` and `import(\`#site/content\`)` (template-literal dynamic import — though this is rare, it is in scope per Req 7.4(d)). - **Allowlist** (path-based): ```ts const ALLOWLIST = new Set([ "src/lib/projects.ts", "src/lib/projects.test.ts", "src/__fixtures__/chokepoint-canary.ts", ]); ``` Repo-root-relative POSIX paths. The allowlist-expansion contract (Req 7.4) lives in `docs/projects-authoring.md` §9 and in a comment at the top of `src/lib/projects.test.ts`. - **CI invocation**: `pnpm test` walks all `.ts`/`.tsx` files under `src/` (excluding `node_modules`, `.next`, `.velite`, AND the allowlist entries) and runs `runChokepointScan(filePath)`. Any non-allowlisted file with non-empty `findings` fails the test. - **Canary test (Req 7.6.h)**: a separate test case invokes `runChokepointScan("src/__fixtures__/chokepoint-canary.ts")` and asserts the returned findings cover all four kinds (`named`, `namespace`, `barrel`, `dynamic`) — at least one of each. This is the test-of-the-test contract from Req 7.6.h. - **Canary fixture** at `src/__fixtures__/chokepoint-canary.ts`: ```ts // Canary fixture for Req 7.4 chokepoint test. Excluded from tsconfig build. // Contains all four forbidden patterns. DO NOT REMOVE — see Req 7.6.h. // eslint-disable import { projects } from "#site/content"; // (a) named import * as content from "#site/content"; // (b) namespace const _ns = content.projects; // (b) namespace member access export { projects as reExported } from "#site/content"; // (c) barrel rename const dyn = import("#site/content"); // (d) dynamic void projects; void _ns; void dyn; ``` - **`tsconfig.json` exclude**: `src/__fixtures__/**` added to `exclude`. The file is NOT type-checked (it intentionally violates the chokepoint), but the scanner traverses it because the scanner reads the source text directly via `fs.readFileSync`. ### Component 12: Build-log warning for `PROJECTS_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1` (Req 7.2.c) - **Purpose**: surface the env-var decision in the build log. - **Location**: inside `getPublishedProjects()` in `src/lib/projects.ts` AND/OR inside the `projects` collection's `.transform()` in `velite.config.ts`. The design CHOOSES the velite-transform path: emit ONE summary line per draft project to `process.stderr` during `velite build`. Rationale: `velite build` runs first in the build sequence; emitting from `getPublishedProjects()` would defer the warning until Next.js's static-generation step and risk silencing in tooling that buffers SSG logs differently. The velite-transform path is the canonical "build" hook. - **Format**: ``` [velite/projects] PROJECTS_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1 is set — including draft project: ``` One line per draft. The line is visible in `vercel logs` for the Build step. - **Reuses**: `process.stderr.write` (already used by the `posts` collection's `BLOG_ALLOW_H4` warning). ### Component 13: `docs/projects-authoring.md` + structural test - **Purpose**: author-facing reference + automated section-heading check. - **Doc location**: `docs/projects-authoring.md` (pinned by Req 11.1). - **Section order (Req 11.1)**: §1 Quick start (copy-paste MDX example) → §2 Frontmatter fields → §3 Cover image constraints → §4 Sharing previews (`ogImage`) → §5 MDX body constraints → §6 Container width and wide media → §7 `updated` editorial guidance → §8 Lifecycle → §9 Local development environment variables → §10 `featured` editorial guidance. - **Structural test** at `docs/projects-authoring.test.ts` (matches repo convention for colocated docs tests; Build fails. - **User Impact**: `velite build` step in CI exits non-zero. The build log names the file, the field, and the constraint that failed. 2. **Cover image dimensions or file size out of bounds (Req 3.1)** - **Handling**: the `.transform()` runs `fs.statSync(coverAbsPath).size`; below 500 KB it does nothing, between 500 KB and 1 MB it writes a warning to `process.stderr`, at 1 MB or above it throws. Dimensions are read from the Velite `s.image()` output and validated against the 1200×800 minima. - **User Impact**: warning surfaces in build log without failing; hard cap fails CI. 3. **`ogImage` aspect or dimension violation (Req 1.3)** - **Handling**: validation in `.transform()`. Throws on `width < 1200` or aspect outside `[1.72, 2.10]`. - **User Impact**: build fails with message naming file and the offending dimension/aspect. 4. **Invalid `links` entry (Req 5.1, 5.2)** - **Handling**: enum/length parsing rejects bad `kind` with the exact Req 5.1 error string. URL validation via `new URL()` + protocol whitelist (`http:`/`https:`) rejects bad URLs. - **User Impact**: build fails with message naming file, array index, bad value, and the escape-hatch hint ("omit 'kind' for a label-only entry with no icon"). 5. **MDX heading-hygiene violation (Req 6.9)** - **Handling**: `checkProjectHeadings()` throws inside the `.transform()`. AST-only — code-fence `

` does NOT trip. - **User Impact**: build fails with named error: `[velite/projects] {file}: first heading must be h2 (found h{depth})` OR `heading skip from h{prev} to h{next}` OR `h{depth} not supported (PROJECTS_ALLOW_H4=1 to override)`. 6. **MDX compile error / reference to undefined component (Req 6.8)** - **Handling**: `s.mdx()` compiles the body; an undefined capitalized JSX reference produces a `ReferenceError` at static-generation time (when `` calls `new Function(code)(runtime)`). Next.js surfaces this as a build failure with the offending slug. - **User Impact**: build fails. Error references slug; author doc §5 explains. 7. **Draft leakage to production (Req 7.3)** - **Handling**: `checkVercelDraftGuard()` throws when `VERCEL=1 + VERCEL_ENV=production + PROJECTS_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1` coexist OR when `VERCEL=1 + VERCEL_ENV=preview` is set WITHOUT `PROJECTS_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1` OR when `VERCEL=1 + VERCEL_ENV` is empty/unrecognized + `PROJECTS_INCLUDE_DRAFTS=1` (looks-like-prod). Production deploys remain unaffected (`PROJECTS_INCLUDE_DRAFTS` is unset). - **User Impact**: build fails at SSG time. Error message names the var combination and the fix path (Vercel env-var scoping). 8. **Slug not found at runtime (Req 6.2)** - **Handling**: `getProjectBySlug()` returns `null`; the page calls `notFound()` → 404. - **User Impact**: visitor sees the site's 404 page. 9. **Empty `content/projects/` directory (Req 1.8, 2.9)** - **Handling**: Velite emits `projects: []`. `getPublishedProjects()` returns `[]`. Gallery page renders empty state. `generateStaticParams()` returns `[]`, so no `[slug]` routes are generated. - **User Impact**: visitor lands on `/projects` and sees "No projects published yet. Check back later." `/projects/` returns 404. 10. **Chokepoint violation (Req 7.4)** - **Handling**: CI test fails. Build does not deploy. - **User Impact**: PR check fails. Author must either route the import through `getPublishedProjects()` OR (legitimate need) add the file to the allowlist in the same PR. 11. **Doc structural-test failure (Req 11.3)** - **Handling**: `docs/projects-authoring.test.ts` fails — a required `##` heading is missing or out of order. - **User Impact**: PR check fails until the doc is fixed. 12. **Lighthouse re-verification miss (Req 12)** - **Handling**: out-of-band — not a build failure. Cadence: after the 3rd, 6th, 9th, … published project. If a re-verification falls below 90, the author opens a follow-up task. - **User Impact**: none at build time. Re-run at every 3rd published project per Req 12. ## Deferrals The following decisions are explicitly deferred and recorded via the `deferrals` MCP tool with `originSpec: project-showcase, originPhase: design`: 1. **Unifying `src/lib/blog-errors.ts` and `src/lib/project-errors.ts`** into a shared `src/lib/content-errors.ts` is deferred. The two modules share ~80% of their content (the `checkVercelDraftGuard` shape) but differ in the env-var name and the error-message text. With only two content types, the duplication is bearable and the unification would force a "name the env-var dynamically" abstraction that obscures the call sites. **Re-evaluation trigger**: when a third content type with the same draft-leak pattern lands (a likely candidate: a future `talks` collection). 2. **TOC component for project detail pages** is deferred — Req 6.6 says h2/h3 get `rehype-slug` IDs but no TOC at launch. **Re-evaluation trigger**: when an author requests a TOC on a project page, or when project bodies routinely exceed ~3 h2 sections. 3. **Tag rendering and tag-route infrastructure** is deferred — Req 2.5 stores tags but renders no chips at launch. **Re-evaluation trigger**: when ≥5 published projects share overlapping tags AND a "related projects" surface becomes desirable. 4. **Custom MDX component registry for projects** is deferred — Req 6.9.d. **Re-evaluation trigger**: when a project requires an interactive demo, screenshot carousel, or other in-MDX component beyond plain markdown. 5. **Automated Lighthouse CI for project pages** is deferred — Req 12. **Re-evaluation trigger**: when a manual re-verification falls below 90, or when the site-wide Lighthouse-CI gate is added in a future infrastructure spec. 6. **OG image generation pipeline** (auto-derived from title/cover) is deferred. At launch, `ogImage` is author-supplied; absence emits the build-time INFO log and falls back to the site default. **Re-evaluation trigger**: when authoring fatigue around manually producing OG variants drives a request for automation. 7. **URL-rename redirects** are deferred — Req 10.4 sets the contract of "Matthew avoids renaming, or adds a manual redirect in `next.config.ts`." **Re-evaluation trigger**: when a published project is renamed and the SEO loss is non-trivial. These deferrals are surfaced as comments in the relevant code locations AND captured in the `deferrals/` registry so future specs can resolve them in sequence.
